title: prusik bounces is cumulative over the whole ledger, so a remedy rewrite's effect is undetectable — one post-fix sprint's few events cannot move a rate computed over dozens of sprints
detail: The remedy-quality loop promises: rewrite the worst remedy, re-run bounces, watch the rate drop. But bounces computes per-class rates over the ENTIRE append-only ledger (17-36 sprints per class). A single post-fix sprint adds about 4 events against a 190-event history, so the rate is mathematically frozen (49 percent before a fix, 49 percent after) and the classes a fix targeted may not even fire in one sprint. Re-running the cumulative view sprint-by-sprint reports the same number for months, so remedy-as-curriculum can never be validated. Fix: add a bounces since-DATE window that filters block events by ts to the sprints run on the fixed engine (adopters know their upgrade date), so a rewrite effect is measured on the post-fix cohort as a clean before/after instead of drowned by history.
repro: prusik bounces before a fix and after one post-fix sprint both report 49 percent wasted (cumulative dilution)

resolution.verify: CUR=$(prusik --version 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+[.][0-9]+[.][0-9]+' | head -1); [ -n "$CUR" ] && [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' '0.214.0' "$CUR" | sort -V | head -1)" = '0.214.0' ] && echo "1 passed: engine carries moat-proven fix fb-efb97d03d9d9 (prusik $CUR >= 0.214.0)"
